name: Ristretto
caffeine: The same dose as an espresso cut early, so slightly less total caffeine than a full shot, not more.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will pull a ristretto on request, and the price.

what: A ristretto is an espresso cut short: the same 18 to 20 g dose stopped at 18 to 30 g, before the bitter, drying end of the shot arrives. The name is Italian for restricted, and it means concentrated, not stronger.
taste: Thick and sweet up front, bright acidity, a short finish and noticeably less bitter than a full shot: syrup rather than coffee.

steps: Grind as for espresso, or a step finer if the bar wants the full 25 to 30 seconds.
Dose 18 to 20 g into a warm double basket and tamp level.
Lock in, pull onto a scale and stop at 18 to 30 g.
Taste for syrup; sour and thin means a step finer.
make.ratio: About 1:1 to 1:1.5, against 1:2 for a normale
make.time: 20 to 25 seconds cut early, 25 to 30 ground finer
make.cup: Warmed demitasse, 2 to 3 oz, a third full

serve: On a saucer with a spoon, straight over; it sits barely a third full, and it is meant to. No water back unless asked: it is two swallows.
story: Ristretto is Italian for restricted. In speciality bars it is a base as much as a drink: the traditional piccolo sits on a single ristretto, and some bars in Australia and New Zealand build a flat white on it.
guest: A ristretto is the first part of an espresso, cut short: thicker, sweeter, less bitter, two sips. I will check the bar can pull one.
watch: Stronger is the trap word: it is more concentrated per sip but carries slightly less caffeine.
The trade disagrees on the words; confirm what the bar means by ristretto.
Send the guest who finds espresso too bitter here, never to a lungo.

recall.prompt: How is a ristretto made, and how does it differ from an espresso?
recall.answer: The same 18 to 20 g dose cut short at 18 to 30 g, about 1:1 to 1:1.5, in a warmed demitasse: thick, sweet, bright, less bitter.

quiz.q: From the same dose, how does a ristretto's total caffeine compare with a normale's?
quiz.explain: Less water through the puck takes slightly less out. It tastes intense only because it is concentrated.

quiz.q: Which dose to yield ratio describes a ristretto?
quiz.explain: A normale runs about 1:2, a lungo 1:3 to 1:4, and 1:15 to 1:18 is filter coffee.

quiz.q: Why does a ristretto taste less bitter than a full shot?
options: It stops before the drying compounds
It is pulled with cooler water
quiz.explain: Acids and sweetness come out first, the bitter, drying compounds last; cutting early leaves those in the puck.

sources.title: Lesson: Sour and bitter are the two directions of extraction
